speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis; have you noticed any changes in your urine color, frequency, or the presence of blood?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: CBC with Differential

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial_Culture: Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the suspicion of pyelonephritis; did you experience any nausea, vomiting, or shaking chills when the fever started? Also, how would you describe the pain—does it radiate to your groin or lower abdomen?

REQUEST TEST: Blood Cultures
REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Pyelonephritis (secondary to prior antibiotic resistance or atypical pathogen despite initial negative imaging).
